reuse.why: Builds getExpectedAmount on the existing getWorstCaseAmount and getApproxNumberThreshold, and routes getScheduledAmount and every server site through it. The server sites still keep their own null-to-0 ternary, even though getScheduledAmount already handles that case.

duplication.why: The approximate rule is written once, and the four inline ranged/number dispatches are removed. The null-to-0 check stays at three sites alongside getScheduledAmount's own null handling.

placement.why: The rule lives in shared/schedules.ts next to getWorstCaseAmount, where the tree keeps schedule amount rules.

scope.why: Focused on the amount rule. The api-models import move and the _amountOp addition to the forecast raw type are small side edits.

maintainability.why: There are now two overlapping entry points (getScheduledAmount and getExpectedAmount). The op parameter is optional and comes after a boolean (`getScheduledAmount(x, false, op)`), so the desktop-client callers of getScheduledAmount (Balance, schedules tables) silently skip the approximate rule.

bypasses_abstraction.where: Server sites call the new shared getExpectedAmount, and getScheduledAmount delegates to it. The remaining inconsistency is client callers not passing op, which is not a bypass of the helper.

disguised_duplication.where: No duplicated logic is introduced; the inline dispatches are replaced by the shared function.

one_place.where: shared/schedules.ts getExpectedAmount, used by preview, forecast, posting, action sync, budget templates and the API (via getScheduledAmount). Client getScheduledAmount callers do not pass op, so they do not apply the approximate rule.
